alwaysSoluble.description: Compounds of these ions are always soluble in water.

rules.note: All Group 1 (alkali metal) cations and ammonium salts are soluble. No exceptions.
All nitrates, nitrites, perchlorates, chlorates, and acetates are soluble. No exceptions.

usuallySoluble.description: Compounds of these ions are usually soluble, with notable exceptions.

rules.note: All halides are soluble EXCEPT those of Ag+, Pb2+, and Hg2^2+ (mercury(I)).
Sulfates are soluble EXCEPT those of Ba2+, Pb2+, Sr2+, and Ca2+ (CaSO4 is slightly soluble).
Fluorides are soluble EXCEPT those of Group 2 (alkaline earth) cations, Pb2+, and a few others.

usuallyInsoluble.description: Compounds of these ions are usually insoluble, with notable exceptions.

rules.note: These anions form insoluble compounds EXCEPT with Group 1 cations and NH4+ (and some with Ca2+, Sr2+, Ba2+ for OH-).
Peroxides are generally unstable in aqueous solution.

summary: ALWAYS soluble: Group 1 salts, NH4+ salts, NO3-, NO2-, ClO4-, ClO3-, CH3COO-
USUALLY soluble: Cl-, Br-, I- (except Ag+, Pb2+, Hg2^2+); SO4^2- (except Ba2+, Pb2+, Sr2+, Ca2+); F- (except Group 2, Pb2+).
USUALLY insoluble: CO3^2-, PO4^3-, CrO4^2-, S^2-, OH- (except Group 1, NH4+).
notes: Solubility at room temperature in water is the default unless specified otherwise.
Slightly soluble compounds are noted as 'usually insoluble' for general chemistry purposes.
Solubility rules apply to aqueous reactions. Some compounds are soluble in non-aqueous solvents.
